chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated, from Muhammad ibn al-Hussein ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanty who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) was asked

By what sign is the Imam recognized after the Imam? He said: Indeed, the Imam has signs: that he be the eldest son of his father after him, and that excellence be in him. And when the caravan arrives in the city, they ask: To whom did so-and-so bequeath? They say: To so-and-so. And the armaments among us are like the Ark among the Children of Israel; it accompanies the Imam wherever he is.

key_terms.التَّابُوت: The Ark (referring to the Ark of the Covenant among the Israelites)

ai.seo_question: What are the signs to recognize the next Imam after the current one?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* establishes the principle of hereditary succession (Nass) within the Ahl al-Bayt, specifying that the Imam is the eldest son of his predecessor and possesses inherent superiority. The analogy of the Tabut (Ark) with the Children of Israel highlights the continuity of divine authority and the physical or spiritual 'armaments' of leadership that accompany the Imam, reinforcing the Shia doctrine of the Imam's infallibility and distinct status.
